skill.name: writing-adrs
skill.description: Prepare one durable architecture decision with real alternatives, consequences, a revisit trigger, stable identity, index changes, and explicit acceptance or supersession. Use when a confirmed choice should outlive the session; do not use for status, tasks, notes, or unconfirmed implementation decisions.
skill.shortDescription: Prepare one durable, indexed, immutable decision record.
skill.defaultPrompt: Use $writing-adrs to determine whether this is a durable decision and prepare the exact proposed record, index, vocabulary, and supersession changes.

instructions: Confirm that the material records one choice among real alternatives whose consequences constrain future architecture or operation.
Identify the user-owned decision content separately from implementation suggestions, task permission, status, and transient context.
Keep the record proposed when the decision content itself has not been explicitly confirmed.
flexibility: Ask for the alternatives, chosen option, or rationale when the durable decision is not yet explicit.
stopConditions: Stop when the material is only information, status, a task, a note, or an unconfirmed recommendation.

instructions: Read the governed decision inventory and relevant accepted records before proposing a new identity.
Treat a changed accepted choice as a new superseding decision rather than an edit to accepted history.
Link related decisions explicitly without copying their rationale into always-on host instructions.
stopConditions: Stop when an existing decision already governs the same choice and no distinct supersession is being proposed.

instructions: Allocate the next collision-free decision identifier across the canonical repository and every discoverable live development checkout.
Treat the repository checker as a merge-time backstop rather than the allocation authority.
Keep the identity stable through review and renumber a later collision before it lands.
stopConditions: Stop when the current decision inventory or concurrent checkout state cannot be inspected sufficiently to avoid a known collision.

instructions: Prepare concise context describing why the choice arose, the selected decision in active voice, and consequences that include costs and constraints.
Include limitations and an explicit revisit trigger that says when supersession would be justified.
Retain Proposed status through every content edit so immutability enforcement cannot freeze an unfinished draft.
flexibility: Wording and emphasis may vary while the alternatives, choice, consequences, limitations, and revisit trigger remain unambiguous.
stopConditions: Stop when the choice, rationale, consequence, or revisit trigger would need to be inferred rather than supplied or confirmed.

instructions: Prepare the exact decision-index entry and verify that it links to the proposed record identity.
When the decision introduces or redefines a term, update the canonical vocabulary owner and every mechanically required reference in the same governed change.
For supersession, restrict the old accepted record change to its exact superseded-status reference.
stopConditions: Stop before landing when the index, vocabulary ownership, related decision, or supersession link is inconsistent.

instructions: Run the complete repository decision and vocabulary checks while the record remains Proposed.
Treat explicit confirmation of the decision content as distinct from permission to perform adjacent work or edit files.
Land the exact proposed record and supporting changes through the governed repository workflow, then record acceptance only at the explicit decision gate.
flexibility: An explicitly confirmed in-session decision may use that confirmation as its content gate when repository policy permits it.
stopConditions: Stop when checks fail, content confirmation is absent, or the exact repository change differs from the reviewed decision packet.

verification: The record captures one real choice, its alternatives, consequences, limitations, and revisit trigger.
No accepted decision body is rewritten; changed accepted choices use explicit supersession.
The decision identifier is collision-free across the currently inspectable repository and development checkouts.
The index, vocabulary registry, related records, and supersession links agree with the proposed record.
Acceptance reflects explicit confirmation of the decision content rather than permission for adjacent implementation work.

gotchas.summary: A decision can introduce or redefine terminology while the canonical vocabulary registry remains unchanged.
gotchas.countermeasure: Update the vocabulary owner and mechanically required references in the same reviewed decision change.

gotchas.summary: Two development branches can allocate the same next decision number after each checks only the primary branch.
gotchas.countermeasure: Inspect discoverable live checkouts during allocation and retain the repository duplicate check as a final backstop.

gotchas.summary: Changing an unfinished draft to Accepted can activate immutability rules before the content is complete.
gotchas.countermeasure: Keep the record Proposed through all content edits and make acceptance the final governed status transition.

gotchas.summary: Permission to continue implementation does not necessarily confirm the architecture decision created during that work.
gotchas.countermeasure: Ask for or retain explicit decision-content confirmation and otherwise leave the record Proposed.

limitations: The guide replaces legacy host-specific paths and branch instructions with governed repository identities and explicit confirmation semantics.
It remains a preview-only candidate and grants no filesystem write, branch, merge, acceptance, execution, effect, readiness, verification, or health authority.
